title: Hello Cloud: First EC2 Instance
tagline: Provision your first compute node in a VPC
briefing: Welcome to CloudCraft! You are the newly appointed Cloud Architect. Your first mission is to deploy a web application server on an AWS EC2 instance. In cloud environments, compute cannot exist in a vacuum—it requires a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), a Public Subnet, and an HTTP inbound security rule.
taskDescription:
1. Place an EC2 instance in the Public Subnet.
2. Connect the Client to the EC2 instance on Port 80.
3. Configure EC2 Security Group to allow Inbound HTTP traffic (Port 80).
docTips: AWS EC2 instances provide scalable computing capacity.
Public subnets have routes to the Internet Gateway.
Default security groups block all inbound traffic unless explicitly permitted.

conceptCard.title: What is a Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)?
conceptCard.summary: Now that you have completed Onboarding, let us look at your private slice of the AWS cloud: a VPC.
conceptCard.analogy: Think of AWS as a massive apartment building, and a VPC as your own private, keycard-locked floor inside that building.
conceptCard.keyTakeaway: Place an EC2 server in the Public Subnet, wire it to Internet Users, and verify Port 80 is open.

requirements.label: Deploy an EC2 instance into Public Subnet
requirements.hint: Select EC2 from the palette and place it inside the cyan Public Subnet grid.

requirements.label: Connect Client traffic to EC2 on Port 80
requirements.hint: Use the Cable Link tool to wire Client to the EC2 server.

requirements.label: Open HTTP Port 80 in Security Group
requirements.hint: Click the EC2 instance and ensure Port 80 is allowed in Inbound Rules.

title: The Internet Gateway (IGW)
tagline: Connect your VPC to the wider world
briefing: A VPC is completely isolated by default. To allow bidirectional communication with the internet, you must attach an Internet Gateway (IGW) and configure the route table with a default route (0.0.0.0/0 pointing to the IGW).
taskDescription:
1. Place an Internet Gateway (IGW) at the VPC boundary.
2. Wire Client -> IGW -> EC2.
3. Configure the IGW default route to 0.0.0.0/0.
docTips: An Internet Gateway is horizontally scaled, redundant, and highly available.
Route table entry 0.0.0.0/0 represents all IPv4 traffic destined outside the VPC.

conceptCard.title: What is an Internet Gateway (IGW)?
conceptCard.summary: A VPC is completely isolated from the outside internet until you attach an Internet Gateway at the edge.
conceptCard.analogy: The Internet Gateway is the main front entrance door to your private office floor. The route "0.0.0.0/0" simply means "send all outside world traffic through this front door."
conceptCard.keyTakeaway: Place an Internet Gateway on the Edge zone (-2, 0) and wire Users -> IGW -> EC2.

requirements.label: Deploy an Internet Gateway (IGW)
requirements.hint: Place an IGW on the edge grid between the external web and VPC.

requirements.label: Route Client traffic through IGW
requirements.hint: Wire Client to IGW, then IGW to EC2.

requirements.label: Route Table has 0.0.0.0/0 pointing to IGW
requirements.hint: Click the IGW and set CIDR Route to 0.0.0.0/0.

title: Subnet Isolation: Public vs Private
tagline: Shield sensitive workloads behind network firewalls
briefing: Never expose databases directly to the internet! Best practice is multi-tier architecture: public subnets host frontend web servers, while private subnets host databases with zero direct inbound internet routes.
taskDescription:
1. Place an RDS Database in the Private Subnet.
2. Connect EC2 Web Server to the RDS Database on PostgreSQL Port 5432.
3. Make sure RDS is NOT directly connected to Client or IGW.
docTips: Private subnets do not have routes to an Internet Gateway.
Only application instances inside the VPC should have access to database ports.

requirements.label: Place RDS Database in the Private Subnet
requirements.hint: Place RDS on the amber/purple Private Subnet area.

requirements.label: Connect EC2 to RDS on Port 5432
requirements.hint: Create a cable link between EC2 and RDS.

requirements.label: Zero direct Internet access to RDS
requirements.hint: Client or IGW must never have a direct cable to RDS.

title: The NAT Gateway Bridge
tagline: Allow outbound patch updates for private servers
briefing: Your private backend instances need security patches (apt update) from the internet, but must remain unreachable from incoming hackers. A NAT (Network Address Translation) Gateway sits in the Public Subnet and translates private requests.
taskDescription:
1. Place a NAT Gateway in the Public Subnet.
2. Connect RDS/Backend to the NAT Gateway for updates.
3. Connect NAT Gateway to IGW.
docTips: NAT Gateways MUST be deployed in a public subnet with an allocated Elastic IP.
NAT Gateway handles one-way outbound traffic: private instances can download patches, but outside traffic cannot initiate connections.

conceptCard.title: What is a NAT Gateway?
conceptCard.summary: Private database servers should never receive incoming calls from strangers on the internet—but they still need to download security updates outbound.
conceptCard.analogy: A NAT Gateway is like a one-way mailroom clerk: your private servers inside the vault can ask the clerk to fetch software updates from outside, but outsiders cannot walk back in.
conceptCard.keyTakeaway: Place a NAT Gateway in the Public Subnet and wire Private DB -> NAT Gateway -> Internet Gateway.

requirements.label: Deploy NAT Gateway in Public Subnet
requirements.hint: Place NAT Gateway in the Public Subnet zone.

requirements.label: Connect NAT Gateway to IGW
requirements.hint: Wire NAT Gateway to the Internet Gateway.

requirements.label: Connect Private Node to NAT Gateway
requirements.hint: Wire the backend/RDS instance to the NAT Gateway.

title: Security Group Defense Matrix
tagline: Lock down attack surface with stateful firewall rules
briefing: An audit revealed your EC2 server has SSH port 22 open to the entire world (0.0.0.0/0)! Malicious bots are trying brute-force attacks. You must restrict SSH to your office bastion IP (203.0.113.50/32) and ensure web traffic (80/443) remains open.
taskDescription:
1. Inspect the EC2 Security Group.
2. Restrict SSH Port 22 source to 203.0.113.50/32.
3. Confirm Port 80 and 443 are allowed for 0.0.0.0/0.
docTips: Never leave SSH (port 22) open to 0.0.0.0/0.
Security Groups are stateful: outbound return traffic is automatically allowed.

requirements.label: SSH Port 22 restricted from 0.0.0.0/0
requirements.hint: Click EC2 -> Change SSH 22 source from 0.0.0.0/0 to 203.0.113.50/32.

requirements.label: HTTP Port 80 is accessible
requirements.hint: Ensure port 80 is allowed in Inbound rules.

iacSnippet:
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "ssh" {
  type        = "ingress"
  from_port   = 22
  to_port     = 22
  protocol    = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks = ["203.0.113.50/32"]
}

title: Application Load Balancer (ALB)
tagline: Evenly distribute traffic across multiple compute nodes
briefing: A single EC2 server is a single point of failure (SPOF). An Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and routes requests across a fleet of targets, continually pinging health checks.
taskDescription:
1. Place an Application Load Balancer (ALB).
2. Place 2 EC2 instances.
3. Wire Client -> ALB, and ALB to both EC2 instances.
4. Enable Target Group Health Check on the ALB.
docTips: ALB distributes traffic using round-robin and least outstanding requests.
Unhealthy targets are automatically removed from receiving traffic.

requirements.label: Deploy an ALB
requirements.hint: Place ALB between the client and compute nodes.

requirements.label: Deploy at least 2 EC2 instances
requirements.hint: Place two EC2 instances to receive balanced load.

requirements.label: ALB wired to Client and both EC2 servers
requirements.hint: Connect Client -> ALB, and ALB -> EC2-1 and EC2-2.

requirements.label: Enable Target Group Health Check
requirements.hint: Click ALB and check Target Group Health Check.

title: Multi-AZ Fault Tolerance
tagline: Survive an entire data center power outage
briefing: AWS Regions consist of multiple isolated Availability Zones (AZs) connected with ultra-low-latency fiber. If lightning strikes AZ-1a, your app must keep running in AZ-1b with zero downtime.
taskDescription:
1. Deploy one EC2 in us-east-1a and one EC2 in us-east-1b.
2. Ensure both are connected to the ALB.
3. Enable Multi-AZ mode on the ALB.
docTips: ALBs must be deployed across at least two Availability Zones.
Cross-Zone Load Balancing evenly distributes requests regardless of instance counts per AZ.

requirements.label: Instances deployed across us-east-1a and us-east-1b
requirements.hint: Place a second EC2 on the bottom half of the grid (Z > 0) for us-east-1b.

requirements.label: ALB Multi-AZ enabled
requirements.hint: Select ALB and toggle Multi-AZ configuration to true.

iacSnippet:
subnets = [
  aws_subnet.us_east_1a.id,
  aws_subnet.us_east_1b.id
]

title: Auto Scaling Group (ASG) Elasticity
tagline: Scale dynamically from Black Friday spikes to midnight calm
briefing: Manual server provisioning fails during viral spikes. An Auto Scaling Group (ASG) dynamically spins up new EC2 instances when CPU exceeds thresholds and terminates idle servers to cut cloud bills.
taskDescription:
1. Deploy an Auto Scaling Group (ASG).
2. Configure Min Capacity to 2 and Max Capacity to 6.
3. Connect ALB to ASG.
docTips: ASG maintains desired capacity and automatically replaces unhealthy instances.
Scale-out policies add instances; scale-in policies remove them with cooldown periods.

conceptCard.title: What is an Auto Scaling Group (ASG)?
conceptCard.summary: Instead of manually adding EC2 servers when traffic spikes, an Auto Scaling Group automatically launches extra servers during busy hours and shuts them down at night.
conceptCard.analogy: Like a grocery store that automatically opens more checkout registers whenever the line gets longer than 3 shoppers.
conceptCard.keyTakeaway: Place an Auto Scaling Group, set Min Capacity to 2 and Max Capacity to 6, and wire it to the Load Balancer.

requirements.label: Deploy an Auto Scaling Group (ASG)
requirements.hint: Place ASG on the grid.

requirements.label: Set ASG Min Capacity >= 2 and Max Capacity >= 6
requirements.hint: Click ASG and configure Min Capacity: 2, Max Capacity: 6.

requirements.label: Connect ALB to ASG
requirements.hint: Create a cable link from ALB to ASG.

title: Path-Based Routing Microservices
tagline: Split /api and /static traffic intelligently
briefing: Instead of monolithic servers, modern architectures route /api requests to compute instances and /static assets to S3 buckets or static web clusters.
taskDescription:
1. Place an S3 Bucket for static files.
2. Connect ALB to both EC2 (for /api) and S3 (for /static).
3. Set S3 static hosting to enabled.
docTips: ALB rules can match Host headers, Path patterns, HTTP headers, and query strings.
Default actions handle unmatched requests.

requirements.label: Deploy an S3 Bucket for static assets
requirements.hint: Place an S3 bucket component.

requirements.label: Connect ALB to S3
requirements.hint: Wire ALB to the S3 bucket.

requirements.label: Enable S3 Static Hosting / CORS
requirements.hint: Click S3 and toggle corsEnabled to true.

title: HTTPS / TLS Offloading with ACM
tagline: Secure web traffic and terminate TLS at the edge
briefing: Unencrypted HTTP traffic exposes user credentials to snooping. Terminate TLS on the ALB using AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to encrypt traffic in transit while freeing backend servers from cryptographic overhead.
taskDescription:
1. Update ALB Port to 443 (HTTPS).
2. Enable Encrypted TLS on ALB.
3. Confirm end-to-end secure transmission to backend EC2.
docTips: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) provisions free, auto-renewing SSL/TLS certificates.
ALB listener redirects port 80 to 443 with HTTP 301 Moved Permanently.

requirements.label: Configure ALB Listener on Port 443
requirements.hint: Click ALB and set Port to 443.

requirements.label: Enable TLS Encryption on ALB
requirements.hint: Click ALB and check Encrypted (ACM TLS).

title: S3 Bucket Security & Public Access Block
tagline: Lock down cloud object storage against data leaks
briefing: Countless corporate data breaches happen due to misconfigured public S3 buckets. AWS now provides "Block Public Access" at the bucket and account level, along with default KMS AES-256 encryption.
taskDescription:
1. Inspect the S3 Bucket.
2. Enable "Block Public Access".
3. Enable "Encrypted" (KMS / AES-256).
docTips: S3 Block Public Access overrides any overly permissive ACLs or Bucket Policies.
Server-side encryption with KMS ensures data is encrypted before saving to disk.

requirements.label: Enable Block Public Access on S3
requirements.hint: Click S3 and toggle Block Public Access to true.

requirements.label: Enable at-rest encryption on S3
requirements.hint: Click S3 and toggle Encrypted to true.

title: RDS Multi-AZ Automated Failover
tagline: Achieve zero-data-loss database redundancy
briefing: Single-node databases crash on hardware failure. RDS Multi-AZ synchronously replicates all database transactions to a standby replica in a second availability zone, automatically failing over in under 60 seconds.
taskDescription:
1. Place an RDS PostgreSQL Database in the Private Subnet.
2. Toggle "Multi-AZ" on the RDS instance.
3. Connect EC2 Web App to RDS on Port 5432.
docTips: Multi-AZ handles OS updates, hardware failures, and AZ outages transparently.
Database endpoint DNS flips automatically during failover with no code change.

requirements.label: Deploy RDS Database in Private Subnet
requirements.hint: Place RDS in the private subnet area.

requirements.label: Enable Multi-AZ on RDS
requirements.hint: Click RDS and toggle Multi-AZ to true.

requirements.label: Connect App to RDS on Port 5432
requirements.hint: Connect EC2 to RDS.

title: RDS Read Replicas for Scale
tagline: Offload read-heavy analytics and dashboard queries
briefing: During analytics batch processing, CPU on your primary database reaches 100%, causing checkout timeouts. Deploy an asynchronous RDS Read Replica to handle read queries, keeping the primary database free for writes.
taskDescription:
1. Configure RDS to enable "Read Replica".
2. Add a second EC2 analytics worker.
3. Wire the analytics worker to the RDS Read Replica.
docTips: Read replicas use asynchronous replication and provide horizontal read scaling.
You can have up to 15 read replicas per primary DB in AWS RDS.

requirements.label: Enable Read Replica on RDS
requirements.hint: Click RDS and toggle Read Replica to true.

requirements.label: Deploy Analytics Worker EC2
requirements.hint: Place a second EC2 instance for analytics.

title: Sub-Millisecond In-Memory Caching
tagline: Protect your SQL database with ElastiCache / DynamoDB Accelerator
briefing: Repeated database lookups for session data and top product catalogs are slow (50ms). Insert a fast NoSQL/in-memory tier between the compute layer and the database to cut latency down to <1ms.
taskDescription:
1. Place DynamoDB / Fast Cache layer.
2. Wire the App Server to the fast data store.
3. Verify traffic flows cleanly.
docTips: Cache-aside pattern: check cache first; on miss, query database and populate cache.
Saves database IOPS and dramatically lowers AWS infrastructure costs.

requirements.label: Deploy Fast In-Memory / NoSQL Data Store
requirements.hint: Place DynamoDB or fast cache layer.

requirements.label: Connect Web App to Caching Tier
requirements.hint: Connect EC2 to DynamoDB / cache.

title: S3 Lifecycle & Glacier Tiering
tagline: Automate data archiving to slash storage bills
briefing: Compliance rules require retaining logs for 7 years, but keeping petabytes of old logs in S3 Standard costs thousands per month. Set up S3 lifecycle rules and versioning to transition objects to Glacier after 90 days.
taskDescription:
1. Click S3 Bucket.
2. Enable "Versioning".
3. Set TTL / transition to 90 days.
4. Enable "Encrypted" at rest.
docTips: S3 Glacier Deep Archive costs as little as $0.00099 per GB/month.
Lifecycle rules automatically transition objects without requiring manual scripts.

requirements.label: Enable S3 Versioning
requirements.hint: Click S3 and toggle versioning to true.

requirements.label: Set S3 TTL / Transition policy to 90 days
requirements.hint: Click S3 and set ttlSeconds to 90.

title: Least-Privilege IAM Roles
tagline: Eliminate hardcoded API keys forever
briefing: Developers put AWS root access keys in application config files, which leaked to GitHub! The remedy: attach an IAM Instance Profile directly to the EC2 server granting least-privilege access (s3:GetObject only) via temporary STS tokens.
taskDescription:
1. Place an IAM Role component.
2. Connect IAM Role to EC2 Server.
3. Configure IAM Role to "s3:ReadOnly" instead of Admin "*".
docTips: EC2 instance metadata service (IMDSv2) delivers auto-rotated temporary credentials.
Never grant AdministratorAccess or "*" when specific action policies suffice.

conceptCard.title: What is an IAM Role?
conceptCard.summary: Hardcoding secret passwords or API keys inside your server code is dangerous—if your code leaks, hackers get full access. IAM Roles attach temporary, tightly scoped permissions directly to a server.
conceptCard.analogy: Instead of giving a contractor the master key to every room in your building ("*"), you hand them a temporary badge that only opens the storage closet ("s3:ReadOnly").
conceptCard.keyTakeaway: Place an IAM Role, wire it to your EC2 server, and make sure its policy is set to "s3:ReadOnly".

requirements.label: Deploy an IAM Role component
requirements.hint: Place IAM Role on the canvas.

requirements.label: Attach IAM Role to EC2 instance
requirements.hint: Wire IAM Role to the EC2 server.

requirements.label: Configure IAM Role for s3:ReadOnly
requirements.hint: Click IAM Role and set iamRole to "s3:ReadOnly".

title: KMS Envelope Encryption
tagline: Cryptographically safeguard sensitive databases at rest
briefing: Regulatory compliance (HIPAA & PCI-DSS) mandates Customer Managed Keys (CMK) with automated annual rotation. Deploy AWS KMS and encrypt both RDS and S3.
taskDescription:
1. Place an AWS KMS Key.
2. Wire KMS to RDS and S3.
3. Ensure both RDS and S3 have "encrypted" set to true.
docTips: AWS KMS uses hardware security modules (HSMs) validated under FIPS 140-2 Cryptographic Module Validation.
Envelope encryption protects data with a Data Encryption Key (DEK) wrapped by a KMS master key.

requirements.label: Deploy an AWS KMS Key
requirements.hint: Place KMS component on the board.

requirements.label: Connect KMS to RDS and S3
requirements.hint: Wire KMS to RDS, and KMS to S3.

requirements.label: Enable Encrypted flag on RDS and S3
requirements.hint: Click RDS and S3 to ensure encrypted is true.

title: AWS WAF: Shielding against DDoS & SQLi
tagline: Inspect Layer 7 HTTP requests before they reach your servers
briefing: A distributed botnet is bombarding your login endpoint with SQL injection payloads (`' OR 1=1;--`). Deploy AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) directly in front of the Application Load Balancer to filter malicious requests.
taskDescription:
1. Place AWS WAF.
2. Wire Client -> WAF -> ALB.
3. Ensure WAF security rule is configured to block malicious traffic.
docTips: AWS WAF integrates seamlessly with ALB, Amazon API Gateway, and CloudFront.
AWS Managed Rules provide out-of-the-box protection against OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities.

requirements.label: Deploy AWS WAF
requirements.hint: Place WAF component on the perimeter.

requirements.label: Route traffic: Client -> WAF -> ALB
requirements.hint: Connect Client to WAF, and WAF to ALB.

title: CloudTrail & Security Audit Guardrails
tagline: Log every single API call across your cloud estate
briefing: Enterprise governance requires immutable audit trails for every API call made by IAM users, root accounts, and automated deployment pipelines. Stream CloudTrail events to an encrypted S3 bucket with MFA delete and versioning.
taskDescription:
1. Connect IAM to CloudWatch telemetry.
2. Ensure S3 Audit bucket has versioning and encryption enabled.
3. Connect CloudWatch to S3 for log persistence.
docTips: CloudTrail records who made what call, when, from which IP, and what parameters were passed.
S3 Object Lock protects against log tampering or rogue deletion.

requirements.label: Deploy CloudWatch / Audit Telemetry
requirements.hint: Place CloudWatch component.

requirements.label: Wire CloudWatch to S3 Audit Bucket
requirements.hint: Connect CloudWatch to S3.

requirements.label: S3 Audit bucket versioned and encrypted
requirements.hint: Click S3 and ensure both versioning and encrypted are true.

title: Zero Trust Network ACL (NACL) Rules
tagline: Stateless subnet boundary packet filtering
briefing: While Security Groups are stateful and operate at the instance level, Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) are stateless and govern traffic across the subnet border. You must enforce subnet rules permitting ephemeral return ports (1024-65535).
taskDescription:
1. Place WAF / Firewall shield in front of EC2.
2. Wire Client -> WAF -> EC2 and confirm clean transmission.
docTips: NACL rules are evaluated in numbered order; lowest number has highest priority.
Because NACLs are stateless, both inbound and outbound rules must be explicitly configured.

requirements.label: Place WAF in front of EC2
requirements.hint: Place WAF between Client and EC2.

requirements.label: Wire Client -> WAF -> EC2
requirements.hint: Connect Client to WAF, then WAF to EC2.

iacSnippet:
resource "aws_network_acl_rule" "ephemeral_return" {
  network_acl_id = aws_network_acl.main.id
  rule_number    = 100
  egress         = true
  protocol       = "tcp"
  rule_action    = "allow"
  cidr_block     = "0.0.0.0/0"
  from_port      = 1024
  to_port        = 65535
}

title: Serverless Compute with AWS Lambda
tagline: Zero idle cost, millisecond auto-scaling compute
briefing: Why pay for an idle EC2 server 24/7 when you only get 50 requests per hour? AWS Lambda runs code on demand with sub-second billing and automatic zero-to-thousands scaling.
taskDescription:
1. Deploy an AWS Lambda function.
2. Wire Client directly to Lambda.
3. Connect Lambda to DynamoDB database for state storage.
docTips: Lambda handles provisioning, patching, OS maintenance, and scaling.
Execution timeout defaults to 3 seconds and caps at 15 minutes.

conceptCard.title: What is Serverless (AWS Lambda)?
conceptCard.summary: With EC2, you pay for the server every hour even if nobody visits your website at 3 AM. AWS Lambda runs your code only for the exact milliseconds a request arrives.
conceptCard.analogy: EC2 is like renting a car 24/7 even when it is parked in your driveway. AWS Lambda is like hailing a taxi and paying only for the 4 minutes you are actually moving.
conceptCard.keyTakeaway: Place an AWS Lambda function and a DynamoDB table, then wire Mobile App -> Lambda -> DynamoDB.

requirements.label: Deploy an AWS Lambda function
requirements.hint: Place Lambda from the palette.

requirements.label: Deploy DynamoDB NoSQL Table
requirements.hint: Place DynamoDB table.

requirements.label: Wire Client -> Lambda -> DynamoDB
requirements.hint: Connect Client to Lambda, then Lambda to DynamoDB.

title: Decoupling with Amazon SQS & DLQ
tagline: Buffer sudden traffic surges and isolate poison pills
briefing: When your flash sale starts, 10,000 checkout requests per second overwhelm your backend database. Decouple producers from consumers using an SQS Queue, and route repeatedly failing messages to a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ).
taskDescription:
1. Place an SQS Queue between the Web Server and Lambda consumer.
2. Wire EC2 -> SQS -> Lambda.
3. Connect Lambda to RDS.
docTips: SQS provides standard (unlimited throughput) and FIFO (guaranteed exactly-once order) queues.
Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ) isolate bad messages without halting the whole queue.

requirements.label: Deploy an SQS Message Queue
requirements.hint: Place SQS component on the grid.

requirements.label: Wire EC2 -> SQS -> Lambda
requirements.hint: Connect EC2 to SQS, then SQS to Lambda.

title: Pub/Sub Fanout with Amazon SNS
tagline: Broadcast a single order event to multiple independent services
briefing: When an order is placed, three separate systems need to react: Email Receipts, Inventory Adjustment, and Fraud Analysis. Instead of point-to-point spaghetti code, publish once to an SNS Topic that fans out to multiple queues or Lambdas.
taskDescription:
1. Place an Amazon SNS Topic.
2. Connect EC2 Web Store to SNS.
3. Connect SNS to two independent Lambda workers.
docTips: Amazon SNS is a managed publish/subscribe messaging service.
SNS can filter messages so subscribers only receive events relevant to them.

requirements.label: Deploy an SNS Topic
requirements.hint: Place SNS from palette.

requirements.label: Connect Web App to SNS Topic
requirements.hint: Wire EC2 to SNS.

requirements.label: Fan out SNS to at least two Lambda workers
requirements.hint: Place two Lambdas and wire SNS to each.

title: DynamoDB Single-Digit Millisecond NoSQL
tagline: Manage hyper-scale key-value data with auto-replication
briefing: Relational databases struggle to scale beyond 50,000 queries per second without complex sharding. DynamoDB provides single-digit millisecond response times at any scale with automatic horizontal partitioning.
taskDescription:
1. Place a DynamoDB Table.
2. Configure DynamoDB encryption and multi-region replication.
3. Connect Lambda API to DynamoDB.
docTips: DynamoDB On-Demand capacity charges only for read/write requests made.
DynamoDB Global Tables provide multi-region active-active database replication in seconds.

requirements.label: Deploy DynamoDB Table
requirements.hint: Place DynamoDB.

requirements.label: Enable DynamoDB KMS Encryption
requirements.hint: Click DynamoDB and set encrypted to true.

requirements.label: Wire Lambda to DynamoDB
requirements.hint: Connect Lambda to DynamoDB.

title: Event-Driven S3 Object Processing
tagline: Auto-trigger image transcoding upon file upload
briefing: When users upload profile photos to S3, an automated event must trigger a serverless Lambda function to generate thumbnails and update the database without polling.
taskDescription:
1. Wire S3 Bucket to Lambda Function.
2. Wire Lambda Function to DynamoDB Table.
3. Configure S3 bucket with CORS enabled.
docTips: S3 Event Notifications can trigger Lambda, SNS, SQS, or EventBridge.
Event-driven architectures eliminate wasteful continuous cron polling.

requirements.label: Connect S3 Event to Lambda
requirements.hint: Wire S3 to Lambda.

requirements.label: Connect Lambda to DynamoDB
requirements.hint: Wire Lambda to DynamoDB.

requirements.label: Enable CORS on S3 Bucket
requirements.hint: Click S3 and toggle corsEnabled to true.

title: Route 53 Hosted Zone & Apex Alias
tagline: Resolve domain names to cloud endpoints with 100% SLA
briefing: Domain Name System (DNS) translates human-friendly names (cloudcraft.io) to IP addresses. Standard CNAME records cannot resolve the apex zone (the bare domain without www). Route 53 Alias records resolve this limitation seamlessly.
taskDescription:
1. Deploy Route 53 DNS Beacon.
2. Connect Client to Route 53.
3. Connect Route 53 to CloudFront or ALB.
docTips: Route 53 is AWS’s highly available and scalable cloud DNS web service with 100% SLA.
Route 53 Alias records recognize AWS resources and auto-update when IPs change.

requirements.label: Deploy Route 53 DNS
requirements.hint: Place Route 53 component.

requirements.label: Wire Client to Route 53
requirements.hint: Connect Client to Route 53.

requirements.label: Wire Route 53 to ALB
requirements.hint: Connect Route 53 to ALB.

title: CloudFront CDN Edge Acceleration
tagline: Deliver content from 450+ Points of Presence worldwide
briefing: Users in Tokyo and London complain that web pages hosted in us-east-1 take 3.5 seconds to load due to transoceanic latency. Deploy Amazon CloudFront to cache static media and API responses at edge locations worldwide.
taskDescription:
1. Place CloudFront CDN at the network edge.
2. Wire Client -> Route 53 -> CloudFront -> S3 Bucket.
3. Configure CloudFront TTL to 3600 seconds.
docTips: CloudFront terminates TLS close to the user and reuses warm connections back to origin.
Saves origin egress bandwidth costs while dropping latency to sub-20ms.

requirements.label: Deploy CloudFront CDN
requirements.hint: Place CloudFront component at the edge.

requirements.label: Wire Route 53 -> CloudFront -> S3
requirements.hint: Connect Route 53 to CloudFront, and CloudFront to S3.

requirements.label: Configure CloudFront Cache TTL to 3600
requirements.hint: Click CloudFront and set ttlSeconds to 3600.

title: CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC)
tagline: Block all direct internet access to your S3 storage origin
briefing: Clever users found your underlying S3 bucket URL (`assets.s3.amazonaws.com`) and are downloading files directly, bypassing CloudFront WAF and caching! Enable Origin Access Control (OAC) so only signed CloudFront requests can read S3.
taskDescription:
1. Click S3 Bucket -> Turn on "Block Public Access".
2. Click CloudFront -> Enable "Origin Access Control (OAC)".
3. Connect CloudFront to S3.
docTips: Origin Access Control (OAC) replaces older Origin Access Identity (OAI) with SigV4 support.

title: Route 53 Latency-Based Routing
tagline: Direct users to the fastest cloud region automatically
briefing: You run instances in US (us-east-1) and Europe (eu-central-1). With Route 53 Latency-Based Routing, DNS automatically responds with the IP address of the data center that yields lowest latency for each querying client.
taskDescription:
1. Click Route 53 -> Set routingPolicy to "latency".
2. Deploy a secondary EC2 node.
3. Wire Route 53 to both compute endpoints.
docTips: Latency routing is based on latency measurements performed by AWS over time.
Combine latency routing with health checks to avoid routing traffic to degraded regions.

requirements.label: Configure Route 53 Routing Policy to "latency"
requirements.hint: Click Route 53 and change routingPolicy to latency.

title: Disaster Recovery Active-Passive Failover
tagline: Seamlessly shift traffic to static backup when primary fails
briefing: If your primary dynamic application fleet experiences a catastrophic outage, Route 53 health checks must detect the 5xx failure and automatically fail over DNS queries to an S3 static maintenance site.
taskDescription:
1. Place S3 Backup Maintenance Bucket.
2. Connect Route 53 to both primary ALB and S3 Backup.
3. Set Route 53 policy to "failover".
docTips: Active-Passive failover provides business continuity during critical incidents.
S3 website hosting serves lightweight apologetic status pages with near-zero running cost.

title: Automated CI/CD Pipeline Build Stage
tagline: From git push to tested container artifact in minutes
briefing: Manual FTP deployments cause midnight outages. A modern DevOps team uses AWS CodePipeline: a webhook captures git commits, AWS CodeBuild executes unit tests and bakes container images, and stores artifacts in S3.
taskDescription:
1. Place an S3 Bucket for deployment artifacts.
2. Connect IAM Deployment Role to EC2 and S3.
3. Configure S3 with versioning enabled for rollback.
docTips: AWS CodePipeline automates your release pipelines for fast and reliable updates.
S3 artifact buckets must have versioning enabled so previous builds can be re-deployed.

conceptCard.title: What is a CI/CD Pipeline?
conceptCard.summary: CI/CD stands for Continuous Integration & Continuous Delivery—an automated conveyor belt that tests your code and deploys it to servers every time you save changes to Git.
conceptCard.analogy: Instead of carrying buckets of water by hand every time you update your app, CI/CD builds a plumbing pipeline that checks water quality and delivers it automatically.
conceptCard.keyTakeaway: Place an S3 Artifact Bucket (with Versioning enabled) and attach an IAM Role to your EC2 server.

requirements.label: Deploy S3 Artifact Store with Versioning

title: Blue/Green Zero-Downtime Deployments
tagline: Shift traffic between twin production fleets without dropping packets
briefing: Updating code in place risks downtime if the app fails to boot. In Blue/Green deployments, a green fleet is provisioned alongside the running blue fleet. The load balancer gradually shifts traffic over once health checks pass.
taskDescription:
1. Deploy Blue EC2 and Green EC2.
2. Wire ALB to both Blue and Green fleets.
3. Enable Target Group Health Check on ALB.
docTips: Blue/Green enables instant rollback by switching the load balancer back to Blue.
Canary deployments route 10% for 5 minutes before full 100% rollout.

requirements.label: Deploy Blue and Green EC2 nodes
requirements.hint: Ensure at least 2 EC2 instances are deployed.

title: Terraform State & S3 Locking
tagline: Manage Infrastructure as Code safely with DynamoDB locks
briefing: When multiple DevOps engineers run `terraform apply` concurrently, state corruption occurs unless state locking is active. Store your `terraform.tfstate` in an encrypted S3 bucket locked with a DynamoDB table.
taskDescription:
1. Place DynamoDB State Lock Table.
2. Connect S3 Terraform Backend to DynamoDB.
3. Ensure S3 bucket is encrypted and versioned.
docTips: Terraform remote backends provide shared access and team collaboration.
DynamoDB `LockID` string prevents two team members from running applies at the same time.

title: Automated Canary Rollback on Alarm
tagline: Automatically abort bad releases before users notice
briefing: Version 2.4 was just pushed to 10% of users, but HTTP 500 errors spiked above 2%! An intelligent CI/CD pipeline triggers an automated CloudWatch metric alarm that tells CodeDeploy to immediately revert traffic to the stable v2.3 release.
taskDescription:
1. Place CloudWatch Monitoring.
2. Configure Alarm Threshold to 2% error rate.
3. Connect CloudWatch to ALB to monitor HTTP error codes.
docTips: Automated rollback prevents prolonged outages during unattended deployments.
Monitor error rate, P99 latency, and CPU metrics during canary windows.

requirements.hint: Click CloudWatch and set alarmThreshold to 2.

requirements.label: Connect CloudWatch to ALB
requirements.hint: Wire CloudWatch to ALB.

iacSnippet:
resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm" "canary_5xx" {
  alarm_name          = "canary-5xx-high"
  comparison_operator = "GreaterThanThreshold"
  evaluation_periods  = 1
  metric_name         = "HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count"
  threshold           = 2
}

title: Immutable Infrastructure & Golden AMIs
tagline: Bake dependencies ahead of time for instant spin-up
briefing: Bootstrapping instances with 15-minute `user_data` shell scripts makes autoscaling too slow during traffic spikes. Instead, pre-bake a hardened Golden Amazon Machine Image (AMI) with all dependencies pre-installed.
taskDescription:

2. Set ASG Min Capacity to 3.

docTips: Immutable servers are never patched in place: to upgrade, deploy fresh instances and destroy old ones.
Reduces instance boot time from 10 minutes to under 45 seconds.

title: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS)
tagline: Orchestrate microservices with enterprise Kubernetes
briefing: Your engineering organization is adopting Kubernetes for container orchestration. Amazon EKS provides a certified conformant Kubernetes control plane managed across multiple availability zones.
taskDescription:

docTips: EKS manages master nodes, etcd, and control plane scaling behind the scenes.
AWS VPC CNI gives every Kubernetes pod its own real VPC IP address.

conceptCard.title: What is Kubernetes (Amazon EKS)?
conceptCard.summary: When an application grows to dozens of small microservices packed into Docker containers, Amazon EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service) organizes, schedules, and heals those containers across servers.
conceptCard.analogy: If Docker containers are standardized shipping crates, Kubernetes (EKS) is the automated cargo ship captain that packs, balances, and replaces crates across the fleet.
conceptCard.keyTakeaway: Place an EKS Cluster between your Load Balancer and your backend RDS Database.

title: Serverless Containers with AWS Fargate
tagline: Run containers without managing or patching underlying EC2 VMs
briefing: Managing EC2 worker nodes (patching OS, sizing AMIs, cluster scaling) wastes hours every sprint. AWS Fargate runs containers serverless: you specify CPU and memory at the task level, and AWS provisions the compute on the fly.
taskDescription:

2. Attach IAM Task Execution Role.
3. Wire ALB directly to Fargate tasks.
docTips: Fargate isolates each task in its own dedicated virtual machine boundary.
No need to pre-allocate cluster capacity or maintain EC2 node groups.

requirements.label: Deploy EKS / Container Cluster
requirements.hint: Place EKS component.

title: Container Image Security with Amazon ECR
tagline: Scan Docker images for CVE vulnerabilities upon push
briefing: Outdated base images carry known CVE vulnerabilities. Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) stores Docker images, scans them against the CVE database on push, and enforces tag immutability so production tags cannot be overwritten.
taskDescription:
1. Place S3 / ECR Storage component.
2. Enable "Encrypted" with KMS.
3. Connect EKS to the container registry.
docTips: ECR Enhanced Scanning powered by Amazon Inspector detects operating system and application package vulnerabilities.
Tag immutability prevents dangerous accidental tag overwrites in production.

title: Kubernetes Pod Horizontal Autoscaling (HPA)
tagline: Scale replica sets based on real-time request metrics
briefing: When incoming traffic surges, Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) queries the Metrics Server and dynamically increases the number of pod replicas to keep response latency low.
taskDescription:

3. Connect EKS to DynamoDB backend.
docTips: HPA scales pods up rapidly and scales down smoothly with stabilization windows.

requirements.hint: Wire CloudWatch to EKS.

requirements.hint: Wire EKS to DynamoDB.

iacSnippet:
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: api-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: api
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 80

title: Service Mesh & Mutual TLS (mTLS)

docTips: Service meshes handle traffic management, observability, and security at the application layer.

tagline: Alert engineers only when real customer impact occurs

tagline: Track request journeys across microservices and spot bottlenecks

taskDescription:

docTips: X-Ray records call trees, exceptions, subsegments, and database latency.
Sampling rules ensure you capture 100% of errors while controlling tracing costs.

resource "aws_xray_sampling_rule" "api_rule" {

tagline: Switch to ARM64 architecture and spare capacity
